title: The text discusses the complex relationship between Black music and politics, highlighting how African music has influenced global music while often being commodified and depoliticized. It emphasizes that despite the commercialization of Black music, it remains a powerful tool for cultural expression and political resistance. The text also critiques the historical suppression of Black artists, using examples like Little Richard and Elvis Presley to illustrate how the music industry has often sidelined Black talent. It concludes by noting the ongoing struggle of Black artists to maintain their cultural identity and contribute to the fight for liberation.
